A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UNEM and contain readable methods, equations, experimental results, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering, relocation, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original UNEM classification results in Tables 1–3, temperature and parameter-sharing ablations, and learned-parameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds ImageNet evaluation, a depth study, cross-dataset evaluation, and CLIP backbone comparisons.

M1.justification: The generalized EM objective, Gaussian and Dirichlet updates, unrolling architecture, learned parameters, and training loss remain unchanged. Added depth and backbone experiments test configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Table 3 expands CLIP evaluation from ten datasets to eleven by adding ImageNet. Appendix D.2 adds transfer scenarios using tiered-ImageNet pre-training with CUB and mini-ImageNet inference, extending coverage within the existing few-shot classification task.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 are retained, including all seven CLIP comparators. New appendix comparisons use the already evaluated PADDLE and EM-Dirichlet methods; no existing corresponding comparison gains or loses a baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments vary depth from 3 to 18 layers, evaluate CLIP ViT-B/32, and use tiered-ImageNet pre-training for five-shot ResNet18 evaluation on other datasets. Existing benchmark settings and the default ten-layer architecture remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D substantially broadens analysis beyond temperature and layerwise parameter learning. New studies examine depth versus accuracy and computational cost, performance under dataset shifts, and dependence on the CLIP backbone (Tables 4, 11, and 12). Original ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report main benchmark averages over 1,000 tasks. v2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Substantial new result blocks cover ImageNet, depth and computational cost, transfer, and ViT-B/32. ImageNet accuracy is 83.1% for UNEM-Dirichlet versus 78.4% for EM-Dirichlet. Transfer results are 72.9% versus 66.0% on CUB and 87.0% versus 82.9% on mini-ImageNet. Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged; Table 3 averages change because ImageNet is added.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A derivations are retained, as are the Gaussian and Dirichlet algorithms in Appendices B–C. Equation relocation and formatting do not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unrolling generalized EM for transductive few-shot learning across vision-only and vision-language models, retaining the same headline gains. Removing 'consistent' from one contribution sentence does not materially redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: The new depth discussion argues that approximately seven to ten layers suffice. Added discussions extend the interpretation of UNEM's advantages to dataset shifts and another CLIP backbone. Existing mechanism explanations and applicability discussion remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents parameter initialization, identifies ResNet50 as the original CLIP backbone, and reports parameter counts and timing measurements. These are disclosures rather than established changes to existing experiments. The stated CLIP initialization scale is not reconciled with the baseline scaling described in Section 4.3.

R1.justification: v2 adds Micaelli and Storkey's gradient-based hyperparameter optimization work and the ImageNet reference by Russakovsky et al. A short related-work addition acknowledges greedy and gradient-based optimization; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized language corrections, an expanded affiliation, and short explanatory additions. Appendix D gains subsections, while the previous D.2 learned-parameter discussion becomes Appendix E. The overall narrative and main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains an ImageNet column, and three new appendix tables are added. Existing tables are renumbered and redistributed, main displays are resized, and Figures 4–5 are separated across pages. Their plotted values and trends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The depth and cost study supports the existing architecture choice, while transfer and backbone comparisons strengthen evidence that its benefits extend beyond the original settings. ImageNet adds useful benchmark coverage. These are meaningful but limited gains to an otherwise stable paper; initialization scaling remains insufficiently explained.
